hints: Identify all four forces acting on the block: weight, normal reaction from table, tension from string, and friction.
Label their directions: weight downwards, normal reaction upwards, tension at $24^\circ$ above the horizontal to the right, and friction horizontally to the left.
walkthrough:
Draw a free-body diagram of the $4\text{ kg}$ block showing all four coplanar forces:
1. Weight $W = 4g = 40\text{ N}$ vertically downwards.
2. Normal contact force $R$ vertically upwards from the table.
3. Tension $T = 30\text{ N}$ directed upwards at $24^\circ$ to the horizontal.
4. Limiting friction force $F$ directed horizontally in the direction opposing the horizontal component of tension.
teacher_walkthrough: To draw the complete free-body diagram of the block:
1. Represent the block as a point or rectangular body on the horizontal table.
2. Add the downward gravitational force (weight): label it $W = 4g\text{ N}$ or $40\text{ N}$.
3. Add the normal reaction force perpendicular to the surface: label it $R$ pointing vertically upwards.
4. Add the applied tension in the string: label it $30\text{ N}$, pointing upwards and to the right at an angle of $24^\circ$ above the horizontal.

5. Add the friction force along the surface: because the horizontal component of tension pulls to the right, friction acts horizontally to the left to maintain equilibrium. Label it $F$ or $F_{\text{friction}}$.

hints: Resolve forces vertically to find the normal reaction: $R + 30\sin 24^\circ = 4g$.
Resolve forces horizontally to find the friction force: $F = 30\cos 24^\circ$.
Because the block is in limiting equilibrium, use $\mu = \frac{F}{R}$.
walkthrough:
Resolve forces vertically in equilibrium with $g = 10\text{ m s}^{-2}$:
$$R + 30\sin 24^\circ = 4(10)$$
$$R = 40 - 30\sin 24^\circ \approx 40 - 12.2029 = 27.7971\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces horizontally in equilibrium:
$$F = 30\cos 24^\circ \approx 27.4064\text{ N}$$

Apply the limiting friction formula $F = \mu R$:
$$\mu = \frac{F}{R} = \frac{30\cos 24^\circ}{40 - 30\sin 24^\circ} = \frac{27.4064}{27.7971} \approx 0.986$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the equilibrium conditions:
$$\sum F_y = 0 \quad \text{and} \quad \sum F_x = 0$$

Resolve forces along the vertical axis:
The upward forces are the normal contact force $R$ and the vertical component of tension $30\sin 24^\circ$.
The downward force is the weight $4g = 4 \times 10 = 40\text{ N}$:
$$R + 30\sin 24^\circ = 40$$
Subtract $30\sin 24^\circ$ from both sides:
$$R = 40 - 30\sin 24^\circ$$
Using $\sin 24^\circ \approx 0.406736$:
$$R = 40 - 12.2021 = 27.7979\text{ N}$$

Resolve forces along the horizontal axis:
The rightward pull is $30\cos 24^\circ$ and the leftward resisting force is friction $F$:
$$F = 30\cos 24^\circ$$
Using $\cos 24^\circ \approx 0.913545$:
$$F = 30 \times 0.913545 = 27.4064\text{ N}$$

Since the block is in limiting equilibrium, the friction is at its maximum value:
$$F = \mu R \implies \mu = \frac{F}{R}$$
